messages:
anya: Heads up — after last night's kernel-selector tweak we see a p99 latency spike on the llama3-13b chat route (hosted). noticed around 22:15 UTC, correlates with increased kernel fallbacks and kv-evict churn. :thinking:

carl: ugh. can you paste the route + model id? any recent config changes besides the selector?

anya: route: /v1/chat/generate (model: r3-13b-std). selector change was to prefer fused-matmul kernel for head_dim==128 but with a relaxed stride check. config snippet: 
```json
{"kernel_selector": {"prefer_fused": true, "stride_threshold": 1.2}}
```

matt: deploy-bot shows the change rolled at 2026-03-17T02:03:00Z. deploy-bot: "deploy r3/runtime:selector-v2 -> prod" :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: new kernel selector applied to pool-llama3-13b-prod (canary -> global).

indra: seeing it in traces too. I took a quick pprof capture on a hot GPU and saw a persistent slow path at the kv cache layer — large memcpy spikes when prefix length + chat template padding > 120 tokens. suspect interaction between padding and kernel stride alignment causing extra copies. attaching short snippet: 
```
# perf summary (hot span)
memcpy: 42%\nmatmul-fused: 18%\nmatmul-slow: 12%\nkv-copy-evict: 22%\n
```

anya: that matches. the chat template we ship adds a 32-token system prompt for some customers, so sequence length distribution shifted. before selector tweak fallback to matmul-fused was rare. now stride heuristic picks fused for head_dim==128 but fused kernel expects contiguous KV layout; padding scatter creates non-contiguous segments so we end up copying into contiguous buffers before invoking kernel -> extra memcpy + eviction.

carl: so two separate knobs: selector stride_threshold and chat-template padding. which is cheaper to change? revert selector or adjust pad behavior?

matt: quick cost estimate from A/B: reverting selector reduces avg p95 by ~12% for this route. reducing pad from 32->8 tokens reduces batch variance but breaks a few canned prompts that rely on long system context. we could also try a per-route override to force slow but contiguous kernel when chat_template_padding>16.

profiling-bot: small reproducer attached: `scripts/repro/llama3_prefixpad_perf.py --model r3-13b-std --prefix-tokens 32 --batch 4 --head-dim 128` (captures nvtx + kernel traces).

indra: another wrinkle — rope_theta default for this model is 8192/512-ish scaling we set; when prefix padding increases effective pos indices, some attention code path takes slightly different memory access pattern (verified in microbench). combination of rope theta scaling + headdim stride mismatch seems to make fused kernel choose a slower tiling variant internally.

anya: proposed plan: 1) roll selector back on prod for r3-13b in 30m (quick revert), 2) land a per-route override that forces contiguous-kernel-choice when chat_template_padding > 16, 3) add a runtime check in selector that simulates `is_padding_scattered` by checking token layout and avoids fused kernel if scatter present, 4) open follow-up to revisit fused kernel to accept scattered inputs or relax copy strategy.

carl: +1 on rollback, we need a hotfix. I'll file the rollback PR.

matt: I'll draft the per-route override change and add unit tests around padding edge cases. also will add a perf test to CI that runs repro script with prefix tokens 0/16/32 at batch sizes 1/4/8.

indra: I'll dig into the kernel traces later today; if we can surface a small patch in fused kernel to tolerate stride mismatch we may avoid copies. also will profile RMSNorm/SiLU overhead — noticed a small regression there when sequence lengths increased (likely memory bound).

anya: thanks team. adding incident label and will notify affected customers. :eyes:

deploy-bot: rollback scheduled: selector-v2 -> selector-v1 for pool-llama3-13b-prod in 30m.
